source.title: GCSE Mathematics 8300 specification
source.note: Read from the official AQA pages on 2026-11-26. Reference statements below are paraphrased for audit use; no AQA paper or mark scheme is included.

foundation.name: Solve problems within mathematics and in other contexts

higher.name: Solve problems within mathematics and in other contexts

domains.name: Ratio, proportion and rates of change

inventory.note: AQA publishes 97 reference statements across six domains. This file inventories all 16 Number references and decomposes them into 35 independently assessable objectives. The decomposition is OpenMind's audit structure, not AQA's sub-numbering, and no teacher has reviewed it. The ladder records what exists, not what the product claims: mapped → content authored → teaching sequence complete → assessment complete → educator reviewed → learner tested → mastery demonstrated.

objectives.statement: Order positive and negative integers, decimals and fractions.
objectives.gap: No AQA-style assessment; no learner evidence.

authoredLesson.note: The listed authored lessons contain all eleven contract parts and are judged to cover this objective. No AQA-style assessment exists.

objectives.statement: Apply the four operations, including formal written methods, to positive and negative integers.

objectives.statement: Apply the four operations to proper and improper fractions.

assessment.markScheme: lib/lessons/authored/fraction-ops.ts#a1, #a3, #a4 and #a5 — 9 marks total: 1 for the addition in a1; 1 for the mixed-number subtraction in a3; 2 for converting and multiplying in a5; 3 for the division method and quotient in a4; 2 for the whole-batch interpretation and 5/12 kg remainder in a4.

requirements.statement: Add proper and improper fractions, including different denominators.
Subtract proper and improper fractions, including different denominators.
Multiply proper and improper fractions.
Divide a mixed number by a proper fraction and express the quotient as a mixed number.
Interpret a fractional quotient in context: state the whole batches and the mass left over.

assessment.note: Four original AQA-style items cover all five published operation requirements: addition (a1), subtraction (a3), multiplication (a5), division (a4), and the interpretation of a quotient in context (a4). Each requirement is assessed by at least one item, but no item has been educator-reviewed or learner-tested, and the difficulty is uncalibrated.

objectives.gap: All five published operation requirements now have an assessment item; no educator review and no learner evidence.

authoredLesson.note: fraction-ops contains the eleven contract parts and explicitly teaches improper fractions, mixed numbers, conversion and the four operations. Its assessment items a1, a3, a4 and a5 cover all five operation requirements; they remain unreviewed and untested.

objectives.statement: Apply the four operations to mixed numbers.
objectives.gap: No AQA-style assessment; no learner evidence.

authoredLesson.note: fraction-ops now contains the eleven contract parts and explicitly teaches improper fractions, mixed numbers, conversion and the four operations. No AQA-style assessment exists.

objectives.statement: Apply the four operations to positive and negative values, including fractions.

requirements.statement: Add and subtract negative fractions after writing them with a common denominator.
Multiply and divide negative fractions, deciding the sign before calculating.
Order negative fractions by position, using a common denominator to compare them.

assessment.note: Three authored items, eight marks; a3 and a4 are structured for partial credit and a5 is a self-marked constructed response.

objectives.gap: The lesson now teaches negative fractions and all three assessment requirements have items. It has not been reviewed by a teacher or tested with learners; the Higher tier still needs a separate check that the concept is offered at the demand that tier expects.

authoredLesson.note: The lesson teaches integers, negative fractions, ordering, all four operations, common misconceptions, guided practice and an eight-mark authored assessment.

objectives.statement: Use the vocabulary and concepts of prime numbers, factors, multiples, common factors, common multiples, HCF and LCM.

authoredLesson.note: factors-primes contains all eleven contract parts and explicitly teaches factor/multiple direction, prime vocabulary, prime factorisation, index notation, uniqueness, HCF and LCM. Its assessment items a1-a7 cover the N4 requirements; they remain unreviewed and untested.

assessment.markScheme: factors-primes a3 (2 marks: factor and multiple), a4 (1 mark: all common factors), a5 (2 marks: HCF and LCM of 9 and 12) and a6 (2 marks: HCF and LCM of 24 and 36) — 7 marks total.

requirements.statement: Use the vocabulary of factors and multiples, including recognising a factor and a multiple of a given number.
Identify all the common factors of two numbers.
Find the highest common factor of two numbers.
Find the lowest common multiple of two numbers.

assessment.note: Four items cover the published N4 factor, multiple, common-factor, common-multiple, HCF and LCM requirements. a3 is a two-row table, so a factor and a multiple are marked independently; a4 requires all the common factors; a5 and a6 ask for HCF and LCM separately. Difficulty is uncalibrated and no item has been educator-reviewed or learner-tested.

objectives.gap: All published N4 factor, multiple, common-factor, common-multiple, HCF and LCM requirements now have an item; no educator review and no learner evidence exist.

assessment.markScheme: factors-primes a1 (1 mark: product of primes), a2 (1 mark: index form) and a7 (2 marks: uniqueness of prime factorisation) — 4 marks total.

requirements.statement: Write a whole number as a product of its prime factors.
Use index notation for a repeated prime factor.
Explain the uniqueness of prime factorisation, apart from the order of the factors.

assessment.note: Three items cover prime factorisation, index notation and uniqueness. a7 is a constructed response and is not machine-marked; it is self-marked against two written criteria. Difficulty is uncalibrated and no item has been educator-reviewed or learner-tested.

objectives.gap: All published prime factorisation, product notation and uniqueness requirements now have an item; no educator review and no learner evidence exist.

objectives.statement: Change recurring decimals into fractions and vice versa (Higher tier).

assessment.markScheme: decimals a3 (3 marks: recurring decimal to fraction), a4 (2 marks: fraction to recurring decimal), a5 (3 marks: why the decimal recurs), a6 (3 marks: why 0.999... = 1) and a7 (3 marks: mixed recurring decimal to fraction) — 14 marks total.

requirements.statement: Change a simple recurring decimal into a fraction.
Change a fraction into a recurring decimal.
Decide from the denominator whether a fraction terminates or recurs, and explain why.
Explain why a recurring decimal such as 0.999... represents an exact rational value.
Change a recurring decimal with a non-repeating first digit into a fraction.

assessment.note: Five items cover recurring-decimal notation, conversion in both directions, the terminating-denominator test, the 0.999... equality and the mixed recurring case. a5 and a6 are constructed responses and are self-marked against written criteria; they are not machine-marked. Difficulty is uncalibrated and no item has been educator-reviewed or learner-tested.

objectives.gap: All published recurring-decimal requirements now have an item; no educator review and no learner evidence exist.

authoredLesson.note: decimals now teaches recurring notation, the denominator test, conversion in both directions and the 0.999... equality alongside terminating decimals. Its assessment items a3-a7 cover the N10 Higher requirements; they remain unreviewed and untested.
